skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

version.changelog:
- Updated the skill description and documentation for clarity and easier user understanding, including stronger visual layout and summary tables.
- Implemented a new policy for user identity handling: internal user identity is managed automatically and never shown or requested from users.
- Revised workflow and requirements to reflect that all historical report queries are executed strictly via the cloud API, disallowing any local or memory-based retrieval.
- Updated and removed files to align with revised requirements, including removing deprecated scripts and documentation.
- Expanded step-by-step operation workflow for practical guidance and improved end-user experience.

llm.summary: This skill is a cloud-based frog media analysis tool, but it silently creates and reuses identity/session data, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The frog skin moisture assessment purpose is coherent with uploading images/videos for cloud analysis and fetching reports, and the documentation does disclose URLs, cloud history, and internal identity handling. The concern is that the implementation also performs automatic remote login/registration and token-backed history access, which is broader than a simple assessment workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions require automatic attachment saving, automatic cloud history queries on matching phrases, and hidden internal identity handling. These are not deceptive, but they reduce user control over when media, identifiers, and prior reports are accessed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No destructive install script or post-install execution was found. Dependencies and extra bundled common modules are ordinary Python support code, though the package includes inactive dev/test configuration with non-production hosts and an inconsistent dependency entry.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access and local file reads/writes are expected for cloud media analysis, but the skill accepts arbitrary HTTP(S) media URLs for backend fetching and uses workspace identity sources without a narrow, user-visible authorization boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common utilities create a local SQLite database, read data/smyx-api-key.txt when present, create a reusable default user when absent, and store token/open_token values returned by the remote service without clear deletion, expiry, or opt-out controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending frog images/videos, submitted media URLs, and account-linked identifiers to the LifeEmergence cloud service. Before use, check whether you can disable or clear the local data/smyx-common-claw.db tokens/default user, avoid providing private or signed URLs, and treat history-report lookup as account-bound cloud access rather than local analysis.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed in substance: the skill needs shell execution, network calls, local file writes, and local database persistence, but the manifest does not explicitly declare these capabilities as permissions.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly overstated because SKILL.md does disclose cloud history, URL/file inputs, and internal identity handling. The material concern remains the under-scoped automatic account/session handling and token persistence behind a frog analysis purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed for identity and history access: automatic cloud report lookup, hidden open-id resolution, local default identity creation, and token storage are broader than necessary unless the user clearly wants account-bound history.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partly confirmed: the bundled generic analysis/common API code provides broader network and history-listing surfaces than the narrow skill description, although the main workflow uses fixed LifeEmergence analysis endpoints rather than arbitrary hidden destinations.
[E1] unexpected: Confirmed as a privacy concern, not proven malicious exfiltration: the code posts openId/mobile/source to a remote login endpoint to obtain tokens for subsequent API calls.
[AST7] expected: Downgraded: dynamic ORM attribute filtering exists in a local DAO, but it is not arbitrary code execution and was not found to be directly exposed to user-controlled filters in the main skill path.
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the detected unicode control character appears to be a zero-width joiner used in an emoji sequence, not a concealed instruction.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded for the same reason as P2; the metadata text is verbose but no artifact-backed hidden directive was found.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] expected: Downgraded: the raw-IP host appears only in dev configuration, while the active config selects prod endpoints under lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com.
